mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month compresses discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both RSAFS and HOUST increase by at least 0.5% over the prior month, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of supply constraints (INDPRO growth below 0.5% annually), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO growth (yoy) is below 0.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In quarters where GDPC1 growth (yoy) is positive, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.5 indicates persistent inflation, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% and UNRATE decreases by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior month, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A reading of industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (relative to 2017=100) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In months where INDPRO is below 100, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases.
